context:
Phase 3 final cleanup and retirement gate. Encapsulates owner decision A4 (defer Windows arm64 keep-vs-drop decision until after validation) and enforces the minimum one-minor-release retention window before removing any legacy generator or C binary.

2026-11-26: after the ADR revision (PR #4540) this decision covers retiring the bundled dbgen/dsdgen binaries and the legacy Python generators once benchbox-datagen is the default everywhere it has a wheel, and keep-vs-drop for Windows arm64.

Owner decisions 2026-11-26 (dialog): (1) PyPI: owner sets up Trusted Publishing once; the agent then tags and publishes 0.x releases when a stage merges and BenchBox needs it. (2) Library repo merges require the review bot (theseus review-verdict/review-gate) and essential CI, mirroring BenchBox. (3) SSB and synthetic acceptance by pre-approved objective criteria: exact row counts, zero orphan FKs, per-column null rate, distinct ratio and mean/quantiles within the legacy generator's 5-seed variation, every query returns rows on both engines where legacy did, exact DuckDB/DataFusion agreement; escalate only on failure. (4) Upstream gaps: implement in benchbox-datagen-core on upstream's public API; upstream PRs are contributions, never waited on; no vendoring. (5) Agent may open tpcgen-rs issues/PRs from the BenchBox-dev fork. (6) Add a Windows arm64 wheel; if it passes the gates, Windows arm64 cuts over too. (7) Cutovers pre-approved when every ADR gate passes; misses go to the owner. (8) Parquet corpus re-baseline once, after the TPC cutover, against library Parquet. (9) Retirement: after all cutovers plus one minor release, remove dbgen/dsdgen and legacy Python generators (qgen/dsqgen under adversarial review). (10) Feature batches: A library TPC; B BenchBox integration; C SSB + 8 synthetic in parallel; D cutovers + re-baseline; E Parquet semantics + DuckLake convert in parallel with A; F retirement.

2026-11-26: replaces the earlier guardrail 'NEVER remove qgen, dsqgen, tpcds.idx, or TPC query templates' — templates and tpcds.idx stay; all binaries go.

description:
## Problem
ADR decisions 7 and 8: after the TPC cutover (data and queries) plus one minor release, BenchBox ships no TPC binaries and no per-OS build.

## Change
Remove dbgen, dsdgen, qgen, dsqgen, benchbox/_binaries/ binaries, compile scripts, Dockerfiles, tpc_compilation.py, the binary identity workflow, the patch stack and the Windows dsqgen retry workaround; keep templates and tpcds.idx. First move the TPC-DS qualification runner (tpcds/qualification/runner.py) to the library; coordinate with crr-v3-qualification-library and crr-v4-official-runs-qualify.

## Decision gates
- Time gate: set not_before to the release date of the first minor release after the TPC cutover; do not start earlier.
- If any replayable bundle fails to replay, or the qualification runner cannot run without C tools, stop and report.
- Historical reproduction is by installing an older BenchBox; if the owner needs more, stop.

## Guardrails
- BenchBox work only in a linked worktree; heavy work only through make heavy-run; never kill processes by name pattern.
- No divergent fork of tpcgen-rs; carried patches only under the 2026-11-27 rule (<= ~200 changed lines, upstream PR, SHA pin, README entry); anything larger goes to the owner with sizes first.
- Human commit identity, no agent attribution. Report only observed results.
